modules.role: Marks the package; it holds nothing else.
Starts `python -m openguildkit` and the installed command; sends a plain `guard --hook` call straight to the guard without importing the rest of the CLI.
The task workflow that the managed block of `AGENTS.md` teaches every agent.
The dependency alert register, from the reports of the project's own scanners.
The `alerts` commands and `task alerts`: import scanner reports and review alerts.
The allow list an organization keeps (MCP servers, models, provider addresses), read by `host scan --allow` and matched against what a project configures.
The `audit` commands: verify the chain of the audit log, and export its events for a SIEM.
The audit log: one JSON event per line, chained by SHA-256, off by default, in a folder the guard protects; verifies the chain and rebuilds events from the records.
Assembles what a brain knows: its specialists' methods, packs and references.

Loads bundled records from `registry/` and project records from `.openguildkit/catalog/`. Rejects unknown fields, duplicate IDs and keys, non-HTTPS sources, multi-line text and pack dependency cycles.
The commands that read the catalog in force: `catalog`, `references`, `patterns`, `brains`, `detect`, `preview`, `recommend` and `update`.
The `check`, `guard` and `host` commands: the project against its profile, the approvals that cover an edit, the host settings.
Gives each problem that `check` and `guard --ci` report a stable rule code, a level and a file, for their SARIF output.
Reads versioned evidence from Git and evaluates the central policy's field check.
Parses commands and runs each one through one table, `COMMANDS`: the module whose `run(command)` runs it, imported for that command only, and what is read before it runs.
What the CLI says when a command ends on an error: the Python trace on request (OPENGUILDKIT_DEBUG=1), and the option that named a file.
What a person sees of the CLI before it runs: the help pages, the options every command shares, and where the global options may be typed.
The two clocks: the date records are written with (`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`) and the real time decisions are made with.
`Command`, what every command module's `run` receives: the arguments, and the project's root, state, catalog and profile, each read once, on first use.
The `completion` command and the reference of the commands (docs/cli.md), both written from the parser: scripts that complete the commands, the options and their values in bash and zsh.
The `integrations`, `mcp`, `ui` and `ci-check` commands, which connect a project to other tools.
Prepares the consultation: scope snapshot, review request and each board's brief with the rules that concern the task.

The controls of OpenGuildKit and the frameworks they may answer: the registry `controls.json`, its validation (a clause only with its source and the day it was read) and the generated tables of `docs/compliance.md`.
Seals an approval to what was approved, verifies signed approvals against the allowed signers in Git, and reads exported records.
Business deliverable templates: inputs, tool actions that need approval, reviewer checks; the architecture decision record filled from a decision task.

The boards' review of the delivered diff (`task diff-review`): each board's brief with the diff since the approved revision, its findings by file and line, and the open points the closing keeps of them.
Proposes components, technologies and versions from the repository's manifests, without running a package manager.
The https address of a documentation page for a message that cites it, at the tag of the installed version (`main` for a source checkout).
The `deliverable` and `docs` commands: drafts from approved tasks, documentation export and its shares.
The one-line forms of the errors a person reads: a file that cannot be opened, in words, and an unknown identifier with the command that lists them.

The `evidence` commands: `export` gathers the decisions with the state of their seal and signature, the profile changes, the history of the signers file, the alerts and the controls of a period into a dossier with a manifest of SHA-256, `verify` recomputes it. Reads the project and states no conformity.
The features: a purpose, its lead tool and three alternatives from the tool registry, and which are on.
The `features` commands: list the features, turn an option on or off through the profile's path.
Runs Git for every module: one place for its options, for a machine without Git, and for file names read with `-z` as they are on disk.
Says whether an approved task covers the work: the host hooks before a request or an edit, and `guard --ci` in a pull request.
The coverage of each host and surface (hook before an edit, approval commands refused), with the pages read; `host check --matrix` prints it and docs/host-coverage.md carries its table.
Writes the settings and hooks a host agent can enforce (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) and reports which rules stay instructions.
Incident response, off by default (#481): a freeze that stops the edit hook and `guard --ci`, and a longest age of an approval, both set with `profile set`.
The `init` command, with its questions at a terminal, and `sync`.
Installs the agent skill and the subagents shipped with this version.
Regular expressions compiled when a command first uses them, so that importing a module compiles none.
The short lane for a change a person declares trivial: the paths it covers, what it never covers (rules, dependencies, the profile, agent instructions) and the one board its paths call for.
Pins the catalog records a project uses in `catalog.lock.json`; `update` shows and applies a newer catalog.
Writes the settings files an administrator deploys by MDM for the managed layer of Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI, and reads back what keeps the hooks of a project from running.
Market dossiers: competitors, dated observations, what is still unknown.
The `market` command: create, fill, check and watch market dossiers.
Stand-in MCP servers over stdio for demos and tests: synthetic answers, no network, no credentials.
Shared stdio transport, handshake and tool dispatch for local MCP servers.

Reads an organization catalog at the commit the catalog lock pins, from a local Git copy and without network; fingerprints the files read and lists the project records that replace one of its records. Off unless a person pins one.
The `org-catalog` commands: show, set (what a commit brings, then the pin a person makes at a terminal), accept a local replacement, off.

Reads the organization policy (`policy.json` of the organization catalog) at the pinned commit, or at the commit `guard --ci --org-policy` is given, and lists where a profile is under its minimum or frozen.
`org-catalog policy`, the lines `check` fails on, the policy a commit brings in `org-catalog set`, and the options of `guard --ci`.
Reads the project's CODEOWNERS with GitHub's syntax and names the owners of the paths a task touches, for the decision brief and the handoff; never written into a record.
Matches the project's stack and context to versioned stack patterns and the packs they apply.
`docs share verify`: signs in to one Documentalist instance with a password typed at the terminal, reads a space's reader invitations and compares their end dates with the share register.

How a profile changes: what each change writes, what weakens a protection, and the one path every change takes, from a command at a terminal or from the web page. Imported by `webui`, `retro` and `features_cli`; no `argparse`.
The `profile` commands: parse a change and confirm at a terminal what weakens a protection; the change itself goes through `profile_changes.py`.
Builds the setup questionnaire, validates the profile, resolves packs, renders the managed block of `AGENTS.md`, computes the profile fingerprint and checks that instructions are current.
Proposes the project's test commands at setup and explains why a check command failed.
Read-only MCP access to the selected project’s profile, rule references, task status and check outcomes.
The `projects` command: several projects at a glance and a search across them; a folder that is not a project, or a project that cannot be read, is named and the others listed. Reads only.
Asks a person at a terminal the setup questions of `init` and the task questions of `task consult`.
Exports verified work as documentation pages for Documentalist and keeps the share register.
The task questionnaire, its follow-ups and the check of the answers.
Searches the reference library, separately from the active rule packs.
Decides which active packs concern a task, from its answers, boards and brief.
The requester of a task (`task new --requested-by`) and the profile option, off by default, that keeps the requester from approving it, at `task decide` and in `guard --ci` (RFC #445).
Records what was delivered for an approved task and the checks that prove it.
The retrospective of a closed task and of the project: what the records already say, counted and never kept, with the profile command a person could type.
Roles by board, off by default (#475): who may clear a board's blockers and approve what a board blocked, set with `profile set approver-roles`.
Routes a task to boards from its brief and answers, then applies required boards and the requester's changes.
Validates and evaluates the machine checks that pack rules declare, without executing anything.
Prints the rule plan as a person reads it, for `preview` and for the confirmation `init` asks (patterns, regulations, packs and conflicts), and the patterns `recommend` preselects.
Writes findings as SARIF 2.1.0 for code scanning: rules with a help link, relative locations, stable fingerprints, the same bytes at every run.
Recognizes credentials and personal data in what people and agents give the CLI.
Quotes the commands printed for a person to paste, the same way for POSIX shells and PowerShell.
Reads declared versions and version ranges for detection, patterns and the Storybook dependency report.
What `__main__` reads before importing the rest of the package: the version, and the guard mode a profile declares.
Writes files atomically, refuses symbolic links, and serialises writing commands with the project lock.
References the company's Storybook, compares it with the project's, and writes extraction proposals.
The `storybook` command: compose, record and extract; loads the Storybook modules only when it runs.
Inventories the components, variants and style tokens of an existing React application.

Lists the agent tools, MCP servers and permissive settings a project shows, and reads its instruction files and settings for hidden characters, phrases that cancel the rules and downloads piped into an interpreter (`host scan`), offline and read-only.

Each task's status without parsing every record, so the edit hook reads only the tasks that can cover an edit, and task list skips the records it does not list and lists closed tasks from the line it kept.
Task records and their state machine, from draft to done, with blockers, approvals and their withdrawal.
The `task` command, from `task new` to `task export`, including the approval a person types at a terminal.
Tells whether standard input is a terminal a person types in: on Windows it must also be a console, not the NUL device.
The tool registry and the MCP servers that connect an agent to each tool; plans and writes host connections.
The `tools` commands: browse the registry, plan and apply MCP connections, call and serve mocks.
The `trace` command: from a file to the exported decisions that cover it, and whether it changed since the last one. Reads only.
The local web interface: serves the built front end and a JSON API over the CLI on 127.0.0.1, refuses what needs a person at a terminal.
The words of the outputs: a count with its noun, in the singular when the count is one.
Checks the boards' review entries and evidence, the deliberation, the decision brief, the blockers and the handoff.
Reads the workstation policy file that an administrator deploys (`/etc/openguildkit/config.json` and its equivalents), for the guard hook and the audit log.
